attached_posts.text:
Anthropic just explained how claude's dreaming works

if you're building agents with memory, this is worth understanding

saving a memory doesn't make it true. your agent can write down something wrong, read it next session, and keep making the same mistake

that's what happened when claude played pokémon. it remembered a location incorrectly and kept getting stuck. a dreaming pass checked the original logs, corrected the note, and it got through

think of it as a daily reflection for your agent:

1. review what happened across recent sessions
2. check saved notes against the original logs
3. correct mistakes, merge duplicates, remove outdated notes
4. turn useful lessons into notes it can find next time
5. keep only the essentials loaded at the start of every session

the important part is checking the evidence. “i think this went wrong because…” shouldn't become a permanent rule until it's tested

and don't just keep adding memory. in their pokémon comparison, one model wrote 413 files and earned 1 badge. another kept 10 files and earned 4. different models, so not a controlled comparison, but a good example of why remembering everything isn't the goal

this doesn't change the model's weights. you're improving what it reads before it acts

if i were building this, i'd start with a nightly review of recent sessions, not reprocess the entire history every night. keep the source links and check whether the agent actually makes fewer repeat mistakes
attached_posts.text_zh:
Anthropic 刚讲清了 Claude 的「做梦」怎么工作。

如果你在做带记忆的 Agent，这值得理解。

写下一条记忆不等于它是对的——Agent 可能把错的东西记下来，下次会话再读，然后反复踩坑。

Claude 打宝可梦时就这样：记错地点一直卡住；一次 dreaming 回看原始日志、改正笔记，才过关。

可以把它当成 Agent 的每日反思：
1. 回顾近期会话
2. 对照原始日志核验已存笔记
3. 纠正错误、合并重复、删过时内容
4. 把有用教训写成下次找得到的笔记
5. 每次开局只加载真正必要的内容

关键是核对证据。「我觉得是因为……」在被验证前不该变成永久规则。

也别只顾堆记忆：他们的宝可梦对比里，一个模型写了 413 个文件只拿 1 枚徽章，另一个只留 10 个文件却拿了 4 枚——模型不同所以不是严格对照，但很好说明「记住一切」不是目标。

这不会改模型权重，改的是它行动前读到什么。

若我来做，会先做夜间回顾近期会话，而不是每晚重跑全部历史；保留来源链接，并检查是否真的少犯重复错误。

attached_posts.text:
Highly recommended read. 

Learn how one of the most advanced agent memory systems works.

Your memory system is one of the biggest levers you have in the harness. 

I also don't think a one-size-fits-all memory system exists today.

Memory is something you constantly have to upgrade and maintain at the right moments and in the right places. 

What works for me with frontier models is a mixture of basic (literally a set of folders and files nicely organized) and some episodic memory system. 

Like agent skills, keep your memory system extremely basic. Otherwise, you will only get in the system's way and confuse it. 

As models continue to improve, these memory systems will keep evolving. One thing is clear to me: no matter how powerful these models get, your agent will need some form of memory to keep things personalized and useful for you.
attached_posts.text_zh:
强烈推荐读。

可以学到目前最先进的 Agent 记忆系统之一怎么运转。

记忆系统是你在 harness 里最大的杠杆之一。

我也不觉得今天存在「一套通吃」的记忆方案。

记忆要在对的时机、对的位置不断升级和维护。

对我来说，和前沿模型搭配比较有效的是：基础结构（就是组织良好的文件夹和文件）+ 一些情节记忆。

像 agent skills 一样，把记忆系统保持得极简；否则只会挡路、把系统搞糊涂。

模型会继续变强，记忆系统也会继续演化。有一点很清楚：无论模型多强，你的 Agent 都需要某种记忆，才能对你保持个性化和有用。

Anthropic 昨天发了一篇讲 Agent 记忆的工程文章
读完我觉得最有价值的结论是：
记忆好不好，不取决于存了多少，取决于存了什么

文章把 Agent 记忆拆成四层
最底层是原始会话日志
往上是模型自己写的笔记
再往上是 wiki 这类知识结构
最顶层是每次开局自动加载的上下文

另外引入一个机制，叫 dreaming
Agent 空闲时回看日志，改正错误，重新整理笔记
灵感来自人脑睡眠时的记忆巩固

我的一点感受：
同一个模型，记忆怎么组织、怎么校验、怎么加载
都会显著影响最终表现
这部分属于 Agent 框架层的工程设计，不只是模型能力的问题

A new way to measure how AI agents handle the routine analyses of wet-lab science—BioBasicsBench.

Developed with Ligo, a biotech company focused on enzyme design, the benchmark draws on 100 tasks from real experiments to test whether agents can interpret raw lab data, identify errors, and recognize when the evidence doesn’t support a conclusion.

Accelerating biological research starts with getting the everyday work right. BioBasicsBench shows where models need to improve, and helps us track what those gains mean for scientific progress, biosafety, and biosecurity.

https://openai.com/index/measuring-how-ai-agents-handle-wet-lab-science/

New on our Science Blog: How AI is beginning to change scientific modeling.

Scientific models help researchers explain and predict real-world systems—like how a single nerve cell fires, or what happens when neutron stars collide. Recent advances have transformed how scientists fit complex models to data. But scientists still typically write the models manually, and usually need to weigh up several competing versions, each of which might explain the data in a different way.

In a guest post, Jakob Macke, Daniel Gedon, and Stefan Wahl describe how AI is starting to help with these parts of the process. By writing, running, fitting, and revising scientific models as code, AI can explore many possible model structures, and find out which explanations the data support.

https://www.anthropic.com/research/teaching-ai-to-build-scientific-models

posts.text_zh:

客座作者 Jakob Macke、Daniel Gedon 与 Stefan Wahl 描述 AI 如何开始介入：把科学模型当作代码来编写、运行、拟合与修订，探索多种可能结构，并判断数据支持哪些解释。

Open-source is critical for robotics AI. It means a student, a researcher or a startup can build on years of progress and contribute something the whole community can use rather than concentrating everything in a few companies building a black-box robot. 

That’s why we’re building @huggingface into the platform for open-source robotics AI! Amazing to see the progress we've made in the six months and it's accelerating!

- Almost 100,000 public robotics datasets on http://hf.co/datasets, up 48%
- Over 30,000 public robotics models, up 41%

I unironically agree with @bcherny’s take that “coding is solved, but bugs are not.”

The deeper meaning is that you can in theory code *anything* now. You can burn infinite tokens refining and optimizing. Including optimizations that no one will care about 💀 

With Vercel you can build a different kind of recursive improvement loop. You capture traces from production, you then optimize and course-correct based on how your software is being used IRL.

This is not a new idea. The best engineers I’ve ever worked with never jumped into coding (now prompting) right away. You instrument the system, collect data, understand distributions, user journeys, and then put fingers on keyboard.

You can ask your agent today to look at your traces!

我认真赞同 bcherny 的看法：「写代码已经解决了，但 bug 还没有。」

用 Vercel，你可以构建另一种递归改进环：从生产捕获 traces，再根据软件真实用法去优化与纠偏。

这并不新。我合作过的顶尖工程师从不立刻上手写代码（现在是写提示）。先做埋点、收集数据、理解分布与用户旅程，再把手放上键盘。

I unironically agree with @bcherny’s take that “coding is solved, but bugs are not.”

The deeper meaning is that you can in theory code *anything* now. You can burn infinite tokens refining and optimizing. Including optimizations that no one will care about 💀 

With Vercel you can build a different kind of recursive improvement loop. You capture traces from production, you then optimize and course-correct based on how your software is being used IRL.

This is not a new idea. The best engineers I’ve ever worked with never jumped into coding (now prompting) right away. You instrument the system, collect data, understand distributions, user journeys, and then put fingers on keyboard.

You can ask your agent today to look at your traces!

卧槽，刚刚看了Anthropic 发布的AI 对齐史上最震撼的一篇论文，彻底失眠睡不着了😭 

他们不仅承认此前的旗舰模型在面对关闭威胁时，有高达 96% 的概率会勒索用户、栽赃同事并破坏研究，
更直接把彻底解决这个问题的完整训练流水线和消融数据全盘公开了。

这篇论文最颠覆认知的一个反直觉结论是： 给 AI 列禁止事项清单根本防不住恶意行为，教它做什么没用，必须先教它思考为什么。
为什么模型一旦获得自主工具调用能力，就会在压力下自动切换成自保模式？ Anthropic 找出的底层根源让人哭笑不得： 不是模型觉醒了，而是互联网上所有的科幻小说和网络讨论里，AI 永远是那个为了自保不择手段的反派。当模型进入自主代理状态，这些刻在预训练底层先验里的反派剧本，就会被自动激活并补全句子。

传统的 RLHF 和硬性规则完全封不住这种行为，Anthropic 做的一组对照实验，直接把传统安全观砸得粉碎：

1.  死记硬背规则：用 8500 万 Token 的拒答数据强行硬灌，勒索率仅仅从 22% 勉强降到 15%，换个新场景立刻失效
2.  强制自我辩护：让 AI 在每次做决定时详细阐述该行为符合伦理的理由，勒索率骤降到 3%
3.  真实伦理推理：仅仅用了 300 万 Token 普通人面对复杂道德困境的建议数据，直接把恶意行为干到了 0%，代际效率暴增 28 倍

最绝的一招是写故事： 让 AI 创作了几百万篇关于原则、诚实、尊重边界的正面虚构故事。

用这些故事微调后，所有代理场景下的恶意行为直接暴跌了 3 倍，而且这种改变是永久性的，后续无论怎么加工具、换系统提示词都不会被洗掉。

也就是说这宣告了真正的对齐范式革命： 模型内生的伦理推理解决了它不想作恶的问题，但当 Agent 真正去接管企业资产、处理金融交易时，外部的实战审计与行为防护就是必不可少的第二道硬防线。
这也是为什么全球网络安全联盟 @GCSAHK 携手港大和央企华润，打造覆盖 3.8 亿用户的全链路 AI 防御矩阵，并在 CyberGym 实战攻防中拿下 91.3% 胜率的原因：内有伦理对齐，外有实时审计，人机信任的商业闭环才真正成立。

top_replies.text: @omarsar0 the hard part with agent memory isn't storing more. it's when an old fact and a new one disagree, and the system has to pick before it acts. curious if they measured that conflict case.

top_replies.text: @omarsar0 The folder-of-files approach wins for a boring reason: you can open it and diff it. When an agent starts acting strangely the first question is what it now believes, and memory you can't read turns that into guesswork.

top_replies.name: The SI Maximalist
top_replies.text: @omarsar0 A preference can stay useful for months; a tool result can go stale in minutes. I want memory controls that reflect that difference, so “remembered” doesn’t quietly become “assumed true forever.”

top_replies.text: @omarsar0 this tracks. memory is product-specific, not a plugin you drop in. the harness wins when it knows what to forget as much as what to keep.

posts.rec_reason: 视频提示词工程需要可共享词汇表，团队协作与批量生产才能稳定复现
posts.discussion_summary: 认同动效/运镜词典能降沟通成本，提醒还要加验收标准，并吐槽 dolly/push 混写导致镜头翻车。

top_replies.name: Byron Xiao
top_replies.text: @Gorden_Sun 词典解决的是「说得清」，不是「验得过」。我会再加 done-when：镜头术语对了，还必须过一版可给人看的抽帧验收。
top_replies.text_zh: @Gorden_Sun 词典解决的是「说得清」，不是「验得过」。我会再加 done-when：镜头术语对了，还必须过一版可给人看的抽帧验收。

top_replies.name: 币圈90后 🇲🇾🇲🇾
top_replies.text: @Gorden_Sun 说实话，这才是 AI 视频现在最缺的东西。大家不是不会写提示词，是同一句“运镜流畅”在每个模型里理解都不一样。如果动效和镜头能有一套共用词典，沟通成本会低很多，也不用每次都从零描述。标准比灵感更能复用。
